name: Isolated Absence or Hypoplasia of Fingers Excluding Thumb, Unilateral
aliases: Unilateral Aplasia/Hypoplasia of Fingers Excluding Thumb

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnosis of Isolated Digital Hypoplasia

criteria.description: Presence of unilateral absence or hypoplasia of fingers excluding the thumb, evident at birth
Radiographic evidence confirming absence or hypoplasia of phalanges in affected fingers without involvement of the thumb
No associated systemic anomalies or syndromic features on clinical and genetic evaluation
Negative or non-contributory family history of limb malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: unilateral absence/hypoplasia of fingers excluding thumb at birth, radiological confirmation, and exclusion of syndromic features.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be performed to exclude syndromic or chromosomal abnormalities.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Duplication of the distal phalanx of the 5th finger

imaging: X-ray showing absence or hypoplasia of phalanges in fingers excluding thumb
MRI to evaluate soft tissue and muscle involvement if indicated
genetic: No known pathogenic variants identified in isolated cases
Genetic testing to exclude syndromic causes recommended
other: Clinical examination confirming unilateral involvement and exclusion of syndromic features

distinguishingFeatures: Usually involves thumb and multiple digits
Often associated with limb defects including thumb

redFlags: Presence of systemic or syndromic features
Progressive neurological deficits in affected limb
references: Orphanet: Isolated absence/hypoplasia of fingers excluding thumb, unilateral (ORPHA:973)
Hunter AGW, et al. Congenital limb anomalies. In: Emery’s Elements of Medical Genetics. 14th ed. 2013.
Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
